title: Deadlock in worker pool task queue
description: A fixed-size worker pool that processes tasks with inter-task dependencies (a task can enqueue a dependent follow-up task and wait for it) deadlocks under load once all workers are blocked waiting on follow-up tasks that have nowhere to run, because the follow-up tasks sit in the same bounded queue behind the blocked workers' own completion.
acceptanceCriteria: A workload where every worker simultaneously enqueues and awaits a dependent task completes without deadlocking.
Pool size and overall queue bounds remain configurable and are not simply removed to avoid the deadlock.
The provided deadlock-reproduction test, which previously hung, now completes within a defined timeout.
Throughput on the existing non-dependent workload benchmark does not regress by more than a documented small margin.
verificationMethod: test-suite: run the deadlock-reproduction test under a hard timeout (must complete, not time out) plus the existing throughput benchmark for regression comparison.
groundTruth: The fix introduces a dedicated priority/reentrant path (or a separate small pool) for dependent follow-up tasks so they are never starved behind the very workers awaiting them, avoiding the circular wait condition.
